runs.text: Christianity is not an improvement or a purification of our old life. Christianity is receiving a completely new life in Christ. As Christians, we become new creatures, born again. This new life is divided into two parts.

The first part is called justification. Justification happens when we accept Jesus as our Savior. When we are justified, we are forgiven for our sins, and the righteousness of Jesus Christ becomes our righteous-ness as a free gift. When we receive this gift by faith, we experience a heart appreciation for God’s gift of salvation.

The second part of becoming a new creature is sanctification. Sanctification is also defined as “holiness.” Holiness is seen in the Christian’s life when we walk in the Spirit. This happens when God’s Holy Spirit lives in us, and produces fruit in our lives. This fruit is listed in Galatians 5:22-24. The fruit of the Spirit includes love, joy, peace, etc. This is how God sets His believers apart for holy use.
We learned in Lesson 2 [J
ustification by Faith

] that the words sanctification, holiness, and fruit of the Spirit are used interchangeably. We would now like to add the word “quicken” (make alive) to the list of words that describe God’s process of sanctification. In Romans 8:11 we discover that God, who raised Jesus from the dead, shall also quicken (make alive) our mortal bodies by His Spirit that dwelleth in us. This quickening is the creative power of God that produces the fruit of holiness and righteousness in our lives. (See also Ephesians 2:4)
GOD’S PURPOSE:
1. What is God’s purpose for the Christian?
1 Peter 2:24
Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree,
that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness:
by whose stripes (wounds) ye were healed.
Note:

God’s purpose for Christians is to individually restore us to the righteousness of His law. (See Romans 8:4) If man were not broken, God may have had a different plan to restore us. But because of man’s inability to repair himself, God has had to intervene. He has given us the righteous life of His Son as our new record or history. (See Galatians 3:24, 27) Next, He went further in His love for mankind and gave the believer the gift of His Spirit to dwell in us. His Spirit produces fruit in our lives. This fruit includes love, which brings our characters back into harmony with the Ten Commandment law.
(QUICKENING) LIFE FROM GOD’S SPIRIT:
2. Why did God make us alive with Christ, even when we were dead in trespasses (sin)?
Ephesians 2:4
But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us
Even when we were dead in sins, hath
quickened
us together with Christ
, (by grace ye are saved).
Note:
The word “quicken” means to make us alive together with Christ. This is a new life from above.
3. Whose Spirit quickens our mortal bodies?
Romans 8:11
But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also
quicken
your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you
Note:

It is God Himself who gives us this life from above. By the same power that God used to raise Jesus from the dead, He gives us a new life from above. The Spirit of Christ now lives in us and is producing a new life in us. We now have different interests than before. We desire the things of God.
4. How does God’s Spirit (quicken) give us life?
John 6:63
It is the spirit that
quickeneth
; the flesh profiteth nothing:
the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life
Note:

It is the quickening power of God that produces a change in the Christian’s life. God quickens us with His words from His Spirit that He gently speaks unto us. No change is seen in man until God’s words are spoken to him. When these words take effect, we begin to see the quickening power of God in our life. We then end up living by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God. (See Matthew 4:4)
SANCTIFIED THROUGH THE SPIRIT:
5. After we are saved by grace through faith, whose workmanship gives us good works?
Ephesians 2:8
For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: 10.
For we are
his workmanship
created in Christ Jesus
unto good works
which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them
Note:
The Bible teaches us that we are re-created unto a new life and good works. These works are God’s works which were before ordained that we should walk in them.
6. Who produces the fruit in our lives?
Galatians 5:22
But the
fruit of the Spirit
is Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith
Meekness, temperance
: against such there is no law.
Note:
God’s Spirit produces the fruit. Our sinful flesh remains wretched.
WALKING IN THE SPIRIT:
7. How do we avoid fulfilling the lust in our lives?
Galatians 5:16
This I say then,
Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh
Note:

We must walk in God’s Spirit. We do this by dying to the lust of the flesh. We do not find success by trying harder with our own willpower and determination. Instead, we find success by dying to the deeds of the flesh, and totally relying on Christ to keep us from sinning. (Jude 1:24)

He will then accomplish His will in all who do not interpose their own perverse will and frustrate His grace. Since our flesh remains unconverted we must through grace mortify (kill) the desires of our flesh.
8. Must we die to self through our own willpower?
Romans 8:13
but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live
Note:

We must die to self and we must repent! But must we repent and die to self in our own power and will? The answer to this question is both yes and no. God will not force our will. With our converted mind we must choose a life with God. Also, we cannot die to self without the assistance of Christ. It is through the Spirit that we mortify (kill) the deeds of the body.

What walking in the Spirit means is: we give Christ permission to have possession of our will. We do this by dying to the desires of the flesh, so He can live in us and produce a life of fruit that is free from sin.
9. What is fulfilled in us who walk in the Spirit?
Romans 8:4
That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit
Note:

The way that we walk in the Spirit is we mortify the flesh through the Spirit. When the flesh is dead, we walk in the Spirit of Christ who then lives in our hearts. Christ’s character is free from sin and is in complete harmony with the Ten Commandments. It will then be said of us: Here are they that keep the Commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. (See Revelation 14:12) Throughout this process our flesh remains sinful, but we do not walk in our flesh. We through grace mortify the flesh and walk in the Spirit.
ABIDING IN THE VINE:
10. Who is the vine?
John 15:5
I am the vine, ye are the branches
: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
Note:
Jesus is the vine, we are the branches. He tells us to abide in Him. The word abide is from the Greek word, “
men’-o
”. It means to continue to remain or dwell in Christ.

Earlier in this study we learned to walk in Christ’s Spirit, vs- walking in our old flesh. When we walk in the Spirit we mortify (put to death) the deeds of our flesh. (See Romans 8:13) Now Jesus is telling us to abide (remain, or continue to walk in Him). We do not have to go back to the old man. We can continue to abide in Him and bring forth much fruit. This fruit is the fruit listed in Galatians 5:22, 23. (Love, joy, peace, gentleness, forgiveness, etc.) This fruit places us in harmony with God’s law as we walk in it. (See Romans 8:4, Galatians 5:23)
11. What abides in us?
John 15:7
If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you
, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.
Note:
“He abideth in me, and I in him”. John 15:5. This is a two way relationship. The believer remains in Christ, and Christ’s life and words remain in the believer.
12. What do we bear when we abide in Christ?
John 15:8
Herein is my Father glorified,
that ye bear much fruit
; so shall ye be my disciples.
Note:
The purpose of the connection to the vine is fruit. Fruit is not self-produced effort. It is the natural result of remaining in the vine.
REPENTANCE:
13. What does seeing the goodness of God lead to?
Romans 2:4
the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance
Note:
As we behold the love and purity of God something happens in our hearts. The goodness of God leads us to repent of our own sinful condition.
14. Who gives repentance to Israel?
Acts 5:31
“Him hath God exalted with His right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, f
or to give repentance
to Israel,
and forgiveness of sins
Note:
We must repent, but the Bible does not teach that the sinner must repent before he can heed the invitation of Christ, “
Come unto Me, all ye that labor and are heavy-laden, and I will give you rest
.” Matthew 11:28. It is the virtue that goes forth from Christ, that leads to genuine repentance. Peter made the matter clear in his statement to the Israelites when he said, “
Him hath God exalted with His right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour,
for to give repentance to Israel
, and forgiveness of sins
.” Acts 5:31. We can no more repent without the Spirit of Christ to awaken the conscience than we can be pardoned without Christ.
Every conviction of our own sinfulness is an evidence that His Spirit is moving upon our hearts.
15. What is the sacrifice of true deep repentance?
P
salms 51:17
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart
, O God, thou wilt not despise.
Note:
When we first come to God and taste of His goodness there is a change that happens in our hearts. Seeing the goodness of God leads us to repentance.
But there is another repentance that lies even deeper. This deeper repentance is the repentance that David felt towards God when he exclaimed, “
Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight
”. Against God alone had he sinned. He acknowledged his sin and it was ever before him. (See Psalm 51:3,4)
David could sense that his whole heart was evil. His plea before God was to; “
create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me
” Psalm 51:4. His acknowledgment was true repentance. It was the repentance of a broken spirit, and a broken and contrite heart.
16. What type of sorrow works true repentance?
2Corinthians 7:10
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of
: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
Note:
Christ brings true repentance. This sorrow is because of hidden sins that has Christ has revealed.
LOVE FULFILLS THE COMMANDMENTS:
17. What are we changed into when we behold the love and glory of the Lord?
2 Corinthians 3:18
But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord
Note:
As we behold God’s love, it changes our hearts. From glory to glory His Spirit changes our selfish hearts to hearts full of His love. Love fulfills the law.
18. What does faith establish when we walk in the Spirit?
Romans 3:31
Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law
Note:
Faith does not make void the law; it establishes the law. In other words, God does more than save us as sinners. His love establishes His law in our hearts.
19. What fulfills the law of God?
Romans 13:10
Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law
Note:

Love is one of the fruit of the Spirit. “Love is the fulfilling of the law”. So as you can see, the law has not been done away with. The only thing that has changed is the way that the law is established. God has made provision for our characters to be brought back into harmony with His law through Christ’s love in our hearts. We need to continue to walk in this love. We must cooperate with the love that Christ brings to our hearts.

One of the many ways to frustrate God’s grace is to keep track of all of the wrongs that others have done to us. Keeping records of wrongs strengthens the perverseness of our flesh and will ultimately frustrate the work of God’s love.

We can often tell when we are walking in our flesh because we begin to feel sorry for ourselves because of the way we feel we are mistreated. The flesh will always feel mistreated. The answer to these feelings is to mortify the flesh through the Spirit of Christ!
20. How do we let our light shine to others?
Isaiah 58:7

Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
Then shall thy light break forth as the morning,
and thine health shall spring forth speedily:
and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy reward
Note:
Sanctification involves dying to sinful desires of the flesh and living by the Spirit. It involves putting to death the deeds of the flesh so that God’s love can shine through us. (See Romans 8:13)
We then cooperate with God by joyfully working to alleviate suffering. Our good deeds are God’s light radiating through us.
True sanctification is God’s work. He alone gets the credit for our good works
Matthew 5:16
Let your light so shine before men
, that they may
see your good works
and glorify your Father which is in heaven
(See James 2:18)
21. Who performs the good works in our life?
Philippians 1:6
Being confident of this very thing,
that he
which hath begun a good work in you
will perform it
until the day of Jesus Christ
Note:
We can be confident knowing that it is God who “performs” good works. Sanctification is God’s work! Jesus is the author and finisher of our faith. (Hebrews 12:2) We cooperate with Him in His work.
THE SABBATH IS A SIGN THAT IT IS THE LORD THAT SANCTIFIES US:
22. What is the sign that it is God who sanctifies us and not our own good works of the flesh?
Exodus 31:13
Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying,
Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign
between me and you throughout your generations;
that ye may know that
I am the LORD that doth sanctify you
Note:

The Sabbath is a sign that it is God who sanctifies us. The Sabbath is a weekly reminder that in our flesh dwelleth no good thing. (See Romans 7:18) It is a sign that we acknowledge our broken spirit, our broken and contrite heart. The Sabbath is a sign that reminds us that it is God alone through His Spirit, not our own determined effort that sanctifies us!

The Spirit of Christ produces a love in our hearts that is in harmony with the Ten Commandments law. The fourth commandment is different from the other nine commandments in that it is not produced by the fruit of God’s Spirit. The Sabbath is a sign that we are asked to “REMEMBER”.
The Fourth Commandment is a sign that it is God who sanctifies us
. We are to “
remember
” the Sabbath day because it is
the Lord who sanctifies us, not our own determined efforts of the flesh

Our part is to cooperate with the grace that God has given us. This is how true Sabbath worship fits into the doctrine of sanctification. Resting in the finished works of Christ produces a final generation of faithful commandment keepers. (See Revelation 14:12.)
God quickens us, He makes us who were dead, alive. He then dwells in us through His spirit. We respond by walking in God’s spirit.
We then continue to live and abide in Him, and produce much fruit. This is the true Sabbath. It is a sign that we acknowledge that it is God who sanctifies us, not our own efforts of our flesh.
23. Will we be keeping the Sabbath on the new earth also?
Isaiah 66:23
From sabbath to sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before me, says the LORD
Note:
In the new earth, God’s people will sing a new song. This song says; “
thou only art holy

” (See Revelation 15:4). We will keep the Sabbath in weekly worship of God through all eternity as a sign that Christ alone deserves praise. We will cast our crowns at his feet remembering that He alone is Holy, He alone deserves worship, He alone is righteous, He alone justified us, it is His Spirit that sanctified us.
24. What do the 24 elders do with their crowns?
Revelation 4:9
And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold
The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever,
and cast their crowns before the throne, saying
Thou art worthy
O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power.
Note:

In the new earth, the redeemed are clothed with white raiment which is the righteousness of Christ. They wear crowns of gold upon their heads, but they know that their righteousness comes from Christ alone. Everything that they have has come as a free gift. They cast their crowns at his feet because He alone is Holy. All that the redeemed have gained has been at His expense and that is the glory of it. We love Him because He first loved us. (See 1 John 4:10)
